title: Spending on securing AI is set to jump almost 70% in 2027
metaTitle: What Gartner's securing AI forecast means for cyber firms
description: Gartner forecasts the market for securing AI will reach almost US$4.8 billion in 2027, up 68.7%, with AI usage control growing fastest, up 73%.
dek: Gartner says traditional security tools often treat AI applications like any other software. I think it's the cyber firms that can explain the risk in plain English that'll win this work.
author: Shane Kennedy

video.title: Securing AI grows almost 70%. IT news worth knowing

shortVersion: Gartner forecasts the market for securing AI will reach almost US$4.8 billion in 2027, up 68.7%, and almost US$7.7 billion by 2028.
It predicts over half of successful attacks on AI agents will exploit access control weaknesses and prompt injection by 2029. AI usage control's tipped to grow fastest in 2027, up 73%.
Two segments are seeing a wave of startups, and Gartner's expecting consolidation to follow. I'd want to be known for explaining the risk in plain English before it gets crowded.

beats.heading: What Gartner forecast
body: Gartner released the forecast in Sydney on 26 August, but it doesn't give an Australian figure. It expects spending on securing AI to reach almost US$4.8 billion in 2027, up 68.7% on this year's US$2.8 billion. By 2028, it forecasts almost US$7.7 billion. That's nearly triple in two years.

Gartner senior principal analyst Shailendra Upadhyay says it's driven by enterprises needing to secure their AI systems and deal with new vulnerabilities. Without enough security and visibility controls, he says, enterprise AI projects "face a high risk of failure".

graphic.eyebrow: The market for securing AI, US dollars
graphic.note: Gartner's estimate for 2026, forecasts for 2027 and 2028

beats.heading: Why the old tools fall short
body: Upadhyay says "traditional security tools often treat AI applications like any other software", and they'll need significant updates to handle AI-specific threats.
He says the need for specialised tools will grow as businesses do more with AI. Autonomous AI's the big one. He expects it'll bring new vulnerabilities "beyond the reach of traditional monitoring".

beats.heading: Where the attacks will land
body: Gartner predicts that by 2029, over half of successful cyberattacks on AI agents will exploit access control weaknesses and prompt injections.
Its advice is to combine existing security systems with specialised AI security tools.

graphic.label: of successful attacks on AI agents will exploit these by 2029, Gartner predicts

beats.heading: The fastest-growing part
body: Gartner splits the market into four main areas: AI application security, AI usage control, AI governance platforms and AI gateways. Application security stays the biggest of the four, at almost US$851 million in 2027.
But it's AI usage control that grows fastest, up 73% to US$749 million. In plain English, that's managing how people across a business use AI tools.

graphic.eyebrow: Securing AI by segment, 2027 forecast, US dollars
graphic.note: Gartner also counts US$2.3B of other securing AI spending

beats.heading: What happens next
body: Gartner doesn't expect every segment to play out the same way. In AI governance platforms and AI gateways, which often build on existing enterprise systems for governance, data and API management, it says major vendors are likely to keep their lead by adding AI features. AI application security and AI usage control are another story. They're seeing a wave of startups.
Upadhyay expects consolidation and acquisitions to follow, with larger cyber security companies buying those startups. So it'll get crowded fast. Then it'll narrow.

beats.heading: What it means for cyber firms
body: What clients will still need is a provider who can explain the risk in plain English and stand behind the result.

Take a 300-person accounting firm that's given its staff an AI assistant. The partners want to know what could go wrong, and who's watching it. They'd probably pick a provider who can answer both on one page, in words they already use, over one with a longer list of features.

graphic.caption: The open padlock gives way to a closed one as it scrolls in

body: Whoever claims that ground first won't be easy to shift.

sources.title: Gartner Forecasts the Market for Securing AI Will Reach $4.8 Billion in 2027

notes: All figures are in US dollars. The 2026 figure is Gartner's estimate, the 2027 and 2028 figures are its forecasts, and the 2029 attack figure is a prediction.
"Managing how people across a business use AI tools" is my plain-English description of AI usage control, not Gartner's wording.
"What it means for cyber firms" and "Shane's take", including the accounting firm example, are my opinion, not Gartner's.
